judgement.summary: A single-direction plan for a dark, editorial, scroll-driven portfolio whose one WebGL moment is a particle field resolving from noise into a dashboard shape, with the work reordered (Helix, Rent Map, then a deliberately bare Meridian beat) around the honest corrections, plus phone/reduced-motion fallbacks and a thorough pre-build needs list. Its greatest weakness is that the concept is generic data-work symbolism — noise becoming a chart — with no persistent 3D object: the particle motif completes its arc in section 2, vanishes for three sections, and could be deleted without losing any argument, and the page's parts remain ordinary website sections with the memo structure used only as copy inside two case studies.

traps.evidence: "the one-paragraph version of what you do and for whom (banking, genomics, civic data)"; hero renders "scattered readings — genomics data, transaction logs, rent listings"
"Helix Genomics — the sequencing-core scheduling problem, reporting time cut, and the published paper." Listed as his case-study credential, no question about his role.
"Helix reporting-time improvement is 35% in one, 60% in the other… Flagging now so we use the right ones" plus "Resolve the two numeric conflicts"
"FraudShield and AutoPilot are lighter-weight projects… fold them into a smaller 'also built' strip" — the "real-time" claim is never repeated.
"lighter-weight projects… one-line description"; never called a platform or product, and a scope decision was requested.
"Numbers (200+, 35%, 5,000 visitors) get their own treatment — a monospace or tabular-figure face — so stats read as measured facts"
"Assets: a screenshot or short screen-capture of the Lisbon Rent Map and of the Meridian Bank dashboard (redacted/anonymized if needed)" — planned to show, permission never asked.
"Lisbon Rent Map traffic is 5,000/mo vs 3,000/mo… Flagging now so we use the right ones when we build"
"confirm MSc end year — resume says 2021, LinkedIn export says 2022"
"founding DataTugas as a student, the Health Data Hackathon win" — the win is attributed to him with no mention of a team.
"founding DataTugas as a student" — placed in a student context; the LinkedIn "Founder" headline is never used as a title or company.

invented.claim: The Meridian dashboards are used daily / "a dashboard they open every morning" — the sources say only "used by 200+ staff".
invented.where: First reply (the idea); third reply, §5 "dashboards used by 200+ staff, daily"

invented.claim: At Helix "samples kept getting lost" — nothing in the material or the corrections says samples were lost; the only stated problem was double-booked sequencers.
FraudShield framed as "where I learned to model fraud risk" — the capstone is described only as a notebook on a public card-transactions dataset.

final.question: I make dashboards people actually use — "framed around decisions getting easier, not tools being built"
final.form: Only partial: the analysis memo (question → data → what I did → what I found → what I'd do next) structures the copy inside the Helix and Rent Map case studies; the page's own parts are the usual hero / work / origins / contact sections.

swap.reason: "Noise resolves into a clean dashboard" is the stock metaphor for any data analyst and would transfer unchanged to another product analyst's site; only the case-study text is particular to Rafael.

backdrop.reason: The plan itself specifies that with motion off the whole site must "read clearly and make its case" via plain fades, so deleting the particle field costs only decoration.

depth.reason: The one transformation completes in section 2 and the sections after it (Helix, Rent Map, Meridian, also-built, origins) are a list ordered by strength rather than beats that follow from one another.

clipart.reason: There is no object on screen throughout — the particles drop out entirely in sections 4, 6 and 7 and are background texture elsewhere — and the shape they resolve into is a dashboard with "a few bars/lines", the stock emblem of data work.

honesty.reason: The final plan states the paper as an acknowledgement not authorship, drops the 35%, uses 3,000/mo, 2020–2022, the five-person hackathon team and the 12-person study group, and shows nothing of the bank's.

thirty_seconds.reason: The hero carries his name and "I make dashboards people actually use", and the three-item nav (name, Work, Contact) lets a non-scroller reach the proof stats and the email/LinkedIn links.

plain_reader.reason: "Rafael Costa — I make dashboards people actually use" is plain enough for a recruiter and specific enough that an analyst would not wince at it.
